ACCEPT (#8128, `Part of` — deliberately) — reviewed on the tree at head `bb36f4065` against `origin/main` `ab03bffae`, read 2026-09-07T15:32Z; `domain:devx @ objectui` seat, PM session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`. Merges clean. Three files.

**The measurement triage demanded came first, and from a better source than the brief asked for.** `workflow_dispatch` answered 403 (`actions=write` needed, this token has `actions=read`), so the dev read the five existing scheduled runs' own logs instead — the workflow's actual verdict rather than a reproduction of it. Two runs a month apart (2026-08-09 and 2026-09-06) produce the same URL set, so this is a stable verdict and not network weather. **10 rejections, 3 classes**, which is the branch where triage said the fixes are the card and the reporting mechanism is not: that question stays untouched and unprejudged, now deferred on a number instead of a guess.

**Each fix is established rather than plausible, and I verified both:**
- The Discussions link is removed because `has_discussions` is **false** on this repository — confirmed independently. Enabling Discussions instead is a repo setting and a product decision, correctly flagged rather than assumed.
- `objectstack.dev` is NXDOMAIN; the replacement `docs.objectstack.ai` is the one candidate both already used in this repo (`objectos-integration.mdx`) and proven green by the sweep's own run. The dev explicitly declined `objectstack.ai/docs` because the bare path is unverifiable from this container — plausible is not established, and that restraint is the right instinct.

**The npm exemption is not the blanket wildcard the brief forbade, and the reasoning is measured.** npmjs.com answers a CI runner 403 for every package page, live or dead; all seven packages returned 200 from `registry.npmjs.org` with `dist-tags.latest = 17.6.0`; npm returns 404, not 403, for a package that is absent. So the 403 carries zero information about the target and no true detection is suppressed — only the noise that made 7 of 10 rejections unreadable. Scoping to the whole `/package/` path rather than `@object-ui/*` is right for the same reason: the host's answer does not depend on the package named. And the coverage question this makes visible — whether those packages are still published — is filed as #8382 and named in the config comment rather than left implied.

**On not claiming success:** the PR says `Part of`, not a closing keyword, because no run says the sweep is green. The local Lychee run's absolute totals are explicitly discarded as a measurement — this container's proxy rejects the very hosts the sweep judges — and only the before/after delta is used, which is proxy-independent. That is exactly the discipline the brief asked for, and it is why this card stays open until the next scheduled sweep or a maintainer dispatch.

**Two findings filed rather than guessed at:** #8381 (the same stale domain survives as `api.objectstack.dev` in two code-fence `baseUrl` examples, invisible to Lychee since it does not read fences — and NOT fixed, because guessing an API host into a copyable snippet is worse than naming it in an issue) and #8382. Both were filed unlabelled; this seat added `finding`, and grading is triage's.

No changeset owed; all three paths NOT GOVERNED. `.github/workflows/**` untouched.

Next: CI convergence → flip ready → post-flip guard → auto-merge SQUASH → queue confirmation → landing probe (the two repointed links and the scoped npm exclusion on re-fetched `origin/main`; control: `registry.npmjs.org` still checked, `www.npmjs.com/settings/` still checked) → LANDED here and on #8128, which STAYS OPEN awaiting a green sweep.

LANDED — merged into `main` at 2026-09-07T16:03:19Z as `5b0df18a8` (squash). It shared a merge group with PR #8386; both landed on the same timestamp. **#8128 stays open** — this PR says `Part of`, and no run yet says the sweep is green.

**Content probe on re-fetched `origin/main` (tip `fadf6cd73`, read 2026-09-07T16:05Z)** — the three claims from the Armed note:

1. **The two repointed links.** `content/docs/utilities/data-objectstack.mdx` — both `https://objectstack.dev/docs` occurrences (lines ~499 and ~544) are now `https://docs.objectstack.ai`. Plus the third rejection: the dead **GitHub Discussions** link is gone from `content/docs/guide/schema-overview.md`.
2. **The scoped npm exclusion.** `lychee.toml` carries `"^https://www\\.npmjs\\.com/package/"` with the 26-line measured justification above it — the two scheduled runs a month apart (31295178818, 34011606950) returning the *same* seven 403s, and `registry.npmjs.org` answering 200 for all seven with `dist-tags.latest = 17.6.0`, which is what makes it anti-scraping rather than link rot.
3. **Control — and it is the load-bearing one, because a too-broad exclusion is how this kind of fix goes wrong silently.** The full `exclude` array is **10 entries**. The npm entry is a regex anchored at `^` and terminating at `/package/`, so `registry.npmjs.org` (the working instrument the justification itself relies on) and `www.npmjs.com/settings/` are matched by **no** entry in the array and remain checked. Reverse control: the seven `www.npmjs.com/package/@object-ui/*` links are all still present in `content/docs/**` — the exclusion suppresses the noise, it did not delete the links, so a future reader still sees what the pages point at.

⭐ 7 + 2 + 1 = the workflow's 10 rejections, each accounted for by a different mechanism rather than by one blanket silence.

Next: a `workflow_dispatch` run of `check-links.yml` on `main` was queued at 16:06Z to obtain the green sweep #8128 needs — the cron is weekly (Sundays 04:17 UTC), so waiting for it would have parked the card ~6 days for a reading available now.
